App.Title: YokoWave
Audio.FileHelp: WAV, MP3 or FLAC; up to 100 MiB. Media playback pauses and stops with this mode.
Audio.LocalHelp: Audio is processed locally. Microphone and system audio are neither recorded nor uploaded.
Audio.SystemHelp: Captures the default playback device on Windows. Microphone and local-file input also support macOS and Linux.
Device.AutoConnectHelp: Reconnect devices previously connected manually. Manual disconnect removes the device from auto-connect. Reconnection keeps output off; pipelines require a manual start.
Device.BluetoothHelp: Disconnect other apps before connecting. Assigned devices are controlled by their mode.
Device.ConnectHelp: Connect to read device status and firmware information.
Device.SimulationHelp: Simulated devices send no Bluetooth commands. Connect a device and set channel levels before starting.
Dg.BalanceHelp: Saved with this mode. Applied on start with the mode’s output limit; edit while stopped. The V3 hardware limit is set to zero on stop and connection.
DgLab.ControllerHelp: Use a controller ID from the relay. Matching nodes in this pipeline share one app connection and expose separate device slots.
DgLab.Error.client_not_found: The paired App is disconnected or unavailable.
DgLab.Error.controller_not_found: The controller ID does not exist. Reconnect the controller and update the invitation ID.
DgLab.Error.duplicate_request_id: The request ID is already pending or the task queue is full.
DgLab.Error.internal_error: The remote app could not execute this request.
DgLab.Error.invalid_operate: This DG-LAB V4 operation is invalid or unsupported by the target device.
DgLab.Error.method_not_found: The remote endpoint does not support this method.
DgLab.Error.slot_not_found: The remote device slot does not exist.
DgLab.RelayHelp: Relays V4 messages without controlling devices. For phone pairing, select a LAN listen address and use a phone-reachable host in the device source.
DgLab.SourceHelp: Scan the QR code with DG-LAB 4 App. Devices appear after pairing. Connection does not start output.

Estim.GentleHelp: Sends a lower hardware strength for the same percentage. Applies to electrical and vibration outputs.
Estim.StrengthHelp: Changes apply to nonzero channels and respect this mode’s output limit. Releasing the boost restores the current automatic level.
Exercise.Help: Movement above the sensitivity threshold resets the waiting interval. Inactivity triggers a timed output, followed by another waiting interval. Higher sensitivity detects smaller angle changes. The timer and manual stop remain available.
Exercise.MovementGoal: Stop when all targets reach the movement goal
Hardware.AuxiliaryHelp: Runs during valid pipeline output. Connecting, pausing and stopping switch it off. Cannot run with motion input.
Hardware.Title: Hardware output options
Help.Data.Clear: Confirming Clear local data stops pipelines, disconnects devices, removes app settings, custom waveforms, graphs, templates and history, then restores defaults. Built-ins and unrelated files remain. Development builds reset recognized older formats; corrupt or unknown versions are preserved and protected from overwriting.
Help.Data.Settings: Language changes apply and save immediately. Save the device source, default new-node limit, global timer maximum and contact visibility in Settings. The default limit applies only to new output nodes. Appearance follows the system sans-serif font, light/dark theme and available accent color.
Help.Data.Storage: Graphs, templates, custom waveforms, settings and history are stored in the local folder shown in Settings. Node edits are retained; save from the context menu or close normally to write graphs. Each session log is limited to 128 KiB with one old file. Cumulative session counts and duration do not decrease when logs roll.
Help.Data.Title: Settings, history and local data
Help.Devices.AutoConnect: Auto-connect is off by default. When enabled, startup discovery and lost links retry devices previously connected manually, with increasing retry intervals after failure. Manual disconnection removes that device from auto-connect. Reconnection starts with output off and does not resume a pipeline. Remote sources must first be connected again.
Help.Devices.Connect: Manage discovery, connections and remote sources in Devices. Pipelines shows only connected devices. Save after choosing Bluetooth or simulation in Settings; changing the source stops pipelines and disconnects current local connections. Simulation sends no Bluetooth commands.
Help.Devices.Hardware: Select a device to edit hardware options in its right-hand details card. Model-specific options include gentle mode, auxiliary motor, hardware channel limits, relative strength and frequency/amplitude balance. Changes save automatically. Options are read-only while the device is reserved. The auxiliary motor cannot be used with motion input.
Help.Devices.Models: Supported devices are YOKONEX electrical V1/V2, vibration and pump devices, DG-LAB Coyote V2/V3, Opossum, and Paw V1.1/Civet input devices. Old Paw V1.0 firmware requires an upgrade. Native Bluetooth currently requires Windows 10 2004 or later; other desktop platforms can use simulation and remote devices.
Help.Devices.Title: Connections and devices
Help.Graph.Disconnect: After stopping, Alt+left-click a connection to remove it, or a port to remove all its connections. Dragging between the same connected ports also removes their connection. Use Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Y to redo, Ctrl+C/V to copy/paste, and Delete to remove the selection. Fit to canvas is in the context menu; right-drag pans.
Help.Graph.Groups: Each device belongs to one pipeline, even while idle. Remove it from that group before assigning it elsewhere. Adding or removing devices leaves nodes, connections and layout unchanged; compatible empty references may be filled automatically. Only devices referenced by nodes participate in a run. Disconnection hides the card but retains grouping and bindings.
Help.Graph.Nodes: Add nodes from the canvas context menu at the pointer position, or use the searchable node library. Drag between ports to connect them and select a node to edit its parameters. Output channel dropdowns list only channels supplied by the device. Starting locks topology, device bindings and grouping; supported live parameters remain editable.
Help.Graph.Saving: Node parameters and lists retain edits without an Apply button. Save from the context menu to write them locally; normal shutdown also saves graphs. Invalid parameter combinations show diagnostics and disable Start until corrected.
Help.Graph.Templates: The pipeline-list context menu can duplicate, save, delete or save as a template; right-clicking a pipeline targets that instance. Expose selected node ports to save a subgraph template. New instances have independent configuration and state, and subgraphs can be expanded for editing. Delete template targets the selected user template in the template dropdown.
Help.Graph.Title: Creating, editing and reusing pipelines
Help.Inputs.AudioSource: Choose a media file, default microphone or Windows system playback. WAV/MP3/FLAC files up to 100 MiB can loop. Inputs open only for Start or explicit calibration. Choose volume/rhythm following and adjust sensitivity; ambient calibration samples about two seconds without starting device output. Speaker volume affects file playback only; analysis continues at 0%.
Help.Inputs.AudioWaiting: Silence, missing/stale audio and media completion zero output while listening continues; fresh frames restore the response. Stop or timer expiry releases input; actual input faults stop the pipeline. Audio is processed locally and live capture is never recorded.
Help.Inputs.Exercise: The device must supply valid angles or steps. Activity restarts the waiting interval; enough inactivity starts a timed output, followed by the next wait. Sensitivity controls the change threshold, and an optional movement goal can end the run. All configured counters must complete; counts are not calibrated walking steps.
Help.Inputs.Restraint: Connect a device sensor to baseline deviation and range mapping. The first valid angle sets that chain’s baseline; recalibrate live as needed. Deviation maps to output. Missing or stale input zeros output until fresh data returns.
Help.Inputs.Simulation: Simulated inputs are marked and may drive only simulated devices. Mapping or boosting retains their simulated origin, so they cannot control real devices. Sensor fields the device has not reported remain unavailable.
Help.Inputs.Sleep: Fixed mode repeats waiting and timed output; random mode chooses intervals, durations, ratios and waveforms within configured ranges and the local pool. Activity-reset mode restarts waiting after fresh movement. A suspended or stalled app restarts the wait rather than replaying missed output. The session timer and Stop remain effective.
Help.Inputs.Strength: Strength progression nodes provide fixed, random and stepped increases. Zero inputs remain zero. Hold the boost button, Space or Enter for a temporary boost; release or focus loss removes it. Reset restarts progression.
Help.Inputs.Title: Touch, audio and sensor pipelines
Help.Inputs.Touch: Use the touch node panel after starting: horizontal position controls 1–100 Hz frequency, vertical position controls 0–100% relative pulse width/amplitude, and connected numeric inputs set base strength. On release choose off, recorded loop or hold. After stopping, name a recording of at least two frames to save it to the waveform library.
Help.Native.Programs: Select a compatible native output program: electrical presets, V2 frequency/pulse-width sequences, motor presets or Coyote V2 raw pulses. Sequence rows can be edited and reordered. Motor presets have only on/off control: nonzero channels and the node limit must be 100%. Use ordinary waveform output for adjustable amplitude.
Help.Native.Pump: The pump template sets peristaltic direction, water-pump on/off and independent durations. Zero seconds means continuous; 1–65535 seconds times each pump separately. Changing one pump resets only its timer. Both timed outputs finishing ends the run; Stop closes both pumps. There is no flow percentage: a zero output-node limit stops pumps, while other ratios do not scale flow.
Help.Native.Title: Native programs and pumps
Help.Output.Readings: Sent-strength bars show the most recent successfully sent, limited command, not measured current. They return to zero after a confirmed stop and show unknown when output cannot be confirmed. Waveform previews show configured curves, not physical measurements.
Help.Output.Timer: Enable the timer and drag the duration slider; arrow keys adjust one second. Starting replaces the toggle and slider with a shrinking progress bar and countdown. Disabling the timer hides the slider/readout, retains the duration and runs until stopped. Timer expiry stops only the current pipeline.
Help.Output.TimerLimit: Set the slider maximum in Settings → Maximum timer duration, from 1–120 minutes. Lowering it shortens longer pipeline durations. Each running pipeline locks its timer; the global maximum is locked while any pipeline is starting or running.
Help.Output.Title: Strength, channels and timing
Help.Output.Values: Strength and node limits use ratios from 0–1: 0.2 is 20% of the device range. Frequency is in Hz. Zero strength may start. Each output/control node has its own limit, applied independently per channel along with hardware limits. Numbers and node limits can be adjusted while running.
Help.Protocol.Commands: When a device is idle, choose and send an action from its protocol panel. Options and ranges depend on the model; queries, lights, step counters, streams, calibration and reset are explicit operations. Saving hardware options does not send a protocol draft. Electrode-contact visibility is configured in Settings.
Help.Protocol.Sensors: Paw V1.1 provides readings, documented triggers, shoulder lights, parameter reset and angle calibration. Parameter ramps may be disabled or set to 1–60 seconds/minutes. Calibration waits three seconds and samples ten seconds; drafts still require sending. Civet provides pressure zeroing and screen orientation. Opossum display sync requires at least 24-byte write capacity (MTU≥27).
Help.Protocol.Title: Protocol actions and sensors
Help.QuickStart.Connect: 1. Choose a device source in Settings and save it, then discover and connect devices in Devices. The first launch uses local simulation.
Help.QuickStart.Create: 2. Select a template in Pipelines and add an instance. Add connected devices to its group. Select each output node, check its device, channel and limit, and connect a number node to its strength input.
Help.QuickStart.Run: 3. Select Start. Strength may begin at zero and be adjusted while running. Stop affects the current pipeline; Stop all or Esc stops every pipeline. Expand a topic below for details.
Help.QuickStart.Title: Quick start
Help.Remote.Client: In Devices on the controlling computer, add a remote source with its name, full endpoint, token and kind, then connect the source and its devices. Remote and local devices can be mixed. Names, endpoints and kinds are saved; tokens and certificate passwords are not, so re-enter them after restart. Lost links or lease expiry attempt to stop the affected output.
Help.Remote.DgLabControlled: To receive V4 control, create a DG-LAB V4 controlled-device or sensor-sharing template. Bind a local Coyote V2/V3, Opossum or Civet, then enter the relay URL and controller ID displayed by the controlling source. Matching nodes in one graph share an App connection. Remote output passes through the local output-node limits. The action and trigger inputs send feedback actions 0–9 on a rising trigger.
Help.Remote.DgLabRelay: The DG-LAB V4 relay template runs without a device. Select its node to set the listen address, port, path, heartbeat, unpaired timeout and optional PFX certificate. Start the graph, then connect the source to its displayed URL. Use a reachable LAN address for phone access. Stopping the relay disconnects its clients; stopping a controlled graph cancels tasks and stops its devices. Native ping interval and allowed unanswered pings are configurable alongside the JSON heartbeat.
Help.Remote.DgLabSource: To control DG-LAB 4 App devices, add a DG-LAB V4 remote source with its relay URL and connect it. Scan the displayed QR code in the App. Paired devices appear in Devices and can be used by ordinary graph nodes. For a phone on the LAN, enter a reachable host before adding the source; the endpoint port and path are retained. This connection uses no token. The selected device details show only App-reported state, including channel status, limits, warm-up and adaptive settings; these rows are read-only.
Help.Remote.Kinds: GATT gives the remote side raw device control; strength limits cannot constrain passthrough commands. High-level control feeds remote output into the local graph for numeric processing, limits and output nodes. The client kind must match its server, and two remote peers cannot reserve the same device at once.
Help.Remote.Server: Connect local devices, then create and bind a WebSocket GATT or high-level control server template. Select its node to set the listen address, port and lease timeout. Start it and use the displayed endpoint and token. The default 127.0.0.1 is local-only. For another computer, listen on a reachable address, configure a client-trusted PFX certificate and use wss.
Help.Remote.Title: Remote sharing and connections
Help.Stop.Behavior: Changing pages, viewing devices or selecting another pipeline does not stop an active run. Stop and timer expiry affect the current pipeline; Stop all, Esc, changing the device source and closing the app stop every pipeline. Saved graphs never start automatically.
Help.Stop.Failure: A disconnect/output fault stops the owning pipeline and its other targets, while unrelated pipelines continue. An unconfirmed stop retains the reservation and reports an error; retry Stop or disconnect/reconnect in Devices. Software cannot confirm physical output after a lost link, and reconnection never restores previous output.
Help.Stop.Title: Stopping, reconnecting and faults
Help.Troubleshooting.Audio: Audio stays at zero: check the selected source, file, input device, system permissions, sensitivity and noise floor. Waiting for fresh data during silence is normal. System playback capture currently requires Windows. A 0% speaker setting does not disable analysis.
Help.Troubleshooting.Output: Run starts but there is no output: check zero-valued numbers, node limits, device/channel bindings, waveform channel definitions and input freshness. Adding a device to a group does not create output nodes. Simulated inputs cannot drive real devices.
Help.Troubleshooting.Remote: Remote connection failed: check that the server pipeline is running, the full host/port, connection kind, token, certificate trust and network reachability. Another computer cannot use 127.0.0.1. Tokens must be provided again after an app restart.
Help.Troubleshooting.Scan: Device not found: check Windows Bluetooth, turn on the device, bring it closer and disconnect other control apps before scanning again. Opossum/Civet may need five power-button presses for discovery. Paw V1.0 requires updated firmware.
Help.Troubleshooting.Storage: Cannot save: preserve and back up the original files in the reported folder, then check write permissions and read errors. Use Clear local data in Settings if you intend to discard that data; do not overwrite unknown-version files as empty data.
Help.Troubleshooting.Title: Troubleshooting
Help.Waveforms.Channels: Waveform nodes show only source channels A/B/C defined by the selected asset, with shared frequency and relative pulse width. A-only waveforms can route one port to multiple device channels. Switching to an asset without a channel zeros it and hides its connections; routes remain and reappear when that channel is defined again.
Help.Waveforms.Library: Create, copy or edit waveforms in the library, including generated curves, custom points and sample sequences. Import/export files or text; each import accepts 1–100 unique identifiers. The 66 built-ins cannot be deleted or overwritten; copy one to edit it. Waveforms still referenced by graphs or templates cannot be deleted. Names follow the app language when provided; the source appears in smaller text.
Help.Waveforms.Live: Select a waveform or playlist node to switch its asset live. Only that node restarts its phase; pipeline timing and strength remain. Ordered/random playback can switch only within its list. General waveforms work with supported electrical/vibration devices, with reduced frequency, direction or channel support where required; physical effects are not guaranteed equivalent.
Help.Waveforms.Playlist: Each playlist node holds up to 100 distinct waveforms and supports repeat, once, ordered and random playback. Add, remove and reorder controls share one action row; lists are locked while running. Output channels may use independent waveform/playlist nodes and phases.
Help.Waveforms.Title: Waveforms and playlists
History.Help: Sessions are stored in compact JSON Lines. Files roll at 128 KiB; one previous file is kept.
Input.MotionHelp: Uses each target device’s accelerometer. Missing or stale data (over 2 seconds) produces zero output. Movement counts represent detected angle changes, not calibrated walking steps.
Mode.Name: Mode name
Mode.NoUnassigned: No connected devices available to assign.
Native.BufferHelp: Each channel contains 1–100 steps. Each step lasts 100 ms, with frequency 1–100 Hz and pulse width 0–100.
Native.MotorHelp: Fixed motor programs provide on/off only. Set the native output node limit to 100%; use waveform output for adjustable intensity.
Native.PresetHelp: Program number per channel; 0 disables the channel. Electrical: 1–16. Motor: up to the reported program count.
Native.PulseHelp: Raw timing and pulse fields. X: 0–31, Y: 0–1023, Z: 0–31. Generic waveforms use the recommended Z ≤ 20 range.
Pipeline.Error.Configuration: Choose a device or correct the node parameters.
Pipeline.Error.Connection: A connection refers to a missing node, port or wrong direction.
Pipeline.Error.Cycle: Connections must not form a cycle.
Pipeline.Error.Device: Connect a device that supports the selected output and channel.
Pipeline.Error.Document: Invalid pipeline document, limit or timer.
Pipeline.Error.DuplicateOutput: A device channel can have only one output node.
Pipeline.Error.Input: Missing, expired or invalid input: output is zero while waiting for valid data.
Pipeline.Error.MultipleSources: An input can have only one source.
Pipeline.Error.NodeId: Node identifiers must be unique and nonempty.
Pipeline.Error.Range: A number is outside the target port range or is not an allowed whole number.
Pipeline.Error.Storage: Unable to read or save pipelines. Existing data was preserved.
Pipeline.Error.UnknownNode: The pipeline contains an unknown node type.
Pipeline.Error.Waveform: The waveform is missing or invalid.
Pipeline.PortHelp: Drag between numeric ports. Strength: 0–1; frequency: Hz. Select a node to edit. Unconnected inputs use defaults. Connected inputs with missing or invalid data inhibit output.
Pipeline.PumpHelp: Direction: 0=off, 1=forward, 2=reverse. Water: 0=off, 1=on. Durations are whole seconds. A timed command is sent when its parameters change.
Pipeline.SimulatedHelp: Simulated numeric input. Real devices reject signals derived from this input.
Pipeline.Title: Pipelines
Playlist.Empty: Add waveforms before starting sequential or random playback.
Playlist.Help: Sequential and random playback use only this ordered list, starting at its first entry. Both channels share the playlist waveform. Up to 100 different waveforms; edit while stopped and save modes to keep the list.
Playlist.SleepHelp: Each random cycle independently chooses A/B waveforms from this local pool. Up to 100 different waveforms. Edit while stopped; save modes to keep the pool.
Playlist.Title: Custom playlist
Protocol.Help: Select an operation and edit its parameters. Drafts are not saved per device. Output programs belong to modes. Configuration is unavailable while a mode owns the device.
Protocol.Title: Protocol controls
ProtocolHelp.Calibrate: Stops the current trigger. Wait 3 seconds, then move through the desired range for 10 seconds. Reported ranges can be applied to a button/motion draft.
ProtocolHelp.Display: Sends the latest reported A/B strengths. Requires a 24-byte payload; automatic synchronization runs when supported.
ProtocolHelp.Indicator: Paw colors 1–6: yellow, red, purple, blue, cyan, green.
ProtocolHelp.Motion: Enabled: true/false. Enabling motion turns the auxiliary motor off.
ProtocolHelp.PawButtonMotion: ButtonEventId/Motion.EventId: 0 disables, 1–24 enables. UseAngles selects XYZ bounds (−128–127, equal bounds ignore that axis); otherwise AccelerationThreshold 0–400 and AccelerationAbove. Debounce: 0–7; MappingRange: 0–255. TriggerOnRelease selects button release. Dynamics has the same ranges as random reaction.
ProtocolHelp.PawLive: Streams button, acceleration, signed XYZ angles and external voltage.
ProtocolHelp.PawProbability: Events: 1–6 unique EventId values (1–24), Probability: 0–200 (0–100%). Excess total above 200 is removed from the last slots first. CooldownSeconds: 0–65535.
ProtocolHelp.PawRandom: Event ID: 1–24. Intervals and reaction window: 1–65535 seconds. Continuous parameter changes: disabled, 1–60 seconds or 1–60 minutes. Immediate trigger increase and cancellation decrease: 0–255.
ProtocolHelp.PawVoltage: EventId: 1–24; HighImpedance: true/false; MinimumRaw/MaximumRaw/MappingRange: 0–255. Maximum external voltage: 3 V; do not charge while using CC1.
ProtocolHelp.Pressure: ResetPressure: true/false; Orientation: Unchanged, Normal, Flipped. Both operations can be sent together.
ProtocolHelp.Query: Query: All or Battery; YOKONEX electrical also ChannelA/ChannelB/AuxiliaryMotor/Steps/Motion/Firmware/Light; motor: Product; Coyote V2: ChannelA/ChannelB. Firmware/Light require electrical V2.
ProtocolHelp.ResetPaw: Resets all event parameters without changing active events.
ProtocolHelp.Shoulder: Color/AlternateColor: 0–7; Blink: Solid, Slow, Fast, Stop. 0 turns the light off.
ProtocolHelp.Steps: Action: Stop, Start (resets count), Reset, Pause, Resume.
ProtocolHelp.Stream: Enable or stop the sensor stream. Paw replaces the current trigger with live data or no trigger and allows indicator colors 1–6. Opossum and Civet use the documented fixed indicator byte 01.
Pump.DurationHelp: 0 follows the session; 1–65535 sets a separate timer for each pump. Changing direction or duration restarts that timer. Pause freezes timers.
Remote.ClientHelp: Choose a connection kind and enter its server URL. GATT and high-level control require a token; DG-LAB V4 shows an App pairing code after connecting.
Remote.DeviceHelp: Remote devices use the same modes and protocol controls as local Bluetooth devices. Disconnecting the endpoint stops its assigned modes.
Remote.Name: Endpoint name
Remote.Title: WebSocket
Restraint.Help: The first valid reading sets the baseline. Output is zero inside the safe angle; beyond it, strength rises across the ramp angle up to the configured base strength. Each target has its own runtime baseline.
Restraint.Recalibrate: Set the current angle as baseline
Settings.AppearanceHelp: Theme and accent color follow system settings and update automatically on supported platforms.
Settings.BluetoothHelp: Scan and connect supported Bluetooth devices. Windows uses native GATT; other desktop platforms require a Bluetooth adapter implementation.
Settings.ClearDataConfirm: Stop all pipelines, disconnect devices, and reset settings, auto-connect records, custom waveforms, pipelines, templates, sessions and statistics. Built-in waveforms remain. Other files are unchanged.
Settings.DefaultLimit: Default strength limit for new output nodes
Settings.Offset: Offset channel B by half a period
Settings.SimulationHelp: Devices and readings are simulated. No Bluetooth commands are sent.
Settings.StorageHelp: Statistics, settings, graphs, user templates, custom waveforms and session logs are stored locally in separate files.
Sleep.Help: Wait, output for the configured duration, then repeat. Random mode draws timing, strength ratios and A/B waveforms from local settings. Movement resets only the waiting phase; pause, stop and the session timer always apply.
Sleep.StrengthRange: Random strength ratio (% of current strength): min / max
Status.AudioCalibrated: Ambient noise floor set to {0:0} dBFS.
Status.CopyBuiltIn: The built-in waveform will be saved as a copy.
Status.Discovered: Simulated devices found: {0}. Real Bluetooth devices were not scanned.
Status.Generated: Waveform JSON generated. Copy it or save it to a file.
Status.Stopped: All device outputs set to zero.
Telemetry.Title: Device readings
Touch.Help: Start a session, then hold and drag. Horizontal: frequency 1–100; vertical: pulse width 0–100. Release behavior follows the selected mode.
Touch.Title: Touch control
Transfer.Help: Use a JSON file or paste JSON. Existing IDs are skipped; built-in waveforms are retained.
Transfer.Placeholder: Paste waveform JSON here, or select Generate JSON
Transfer.Title: Import and export
Wave.EditorPreview: Editor preview · shown for valid parameters
Wave.LibraryHelp: Select a waveform to preview it. Copy built-ins, edit custom waveforms, or import and export JSON.
Wave.Name: Name
Wave.PointsHelp: Custom samples · values from 0 to 1, separated by commas
